chunks: Ziyād ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abū al-Ward:
That Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked, while I was with him, about a man who said to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," one hundred times,
So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: "Is he able, for each time, to free a slave?" He said: "No."
He said: "Is he able to feed sixty needy persons one hundred times?"
He said: "Then is he able to fast two consecutive months one hundred times?"
He said: "They are to be separated."

key_terms.إِطْعَامَ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً: feeding sixty needy persons as expiation
key_terms.صِيَامَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: fasting two consecutive months as expiation
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: the formula of ẓihār, likening one's wife to one's mother in prohibition
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: the spouses are to be separated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man performs ẓihār repeatedly and cannot offer the required expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning repeated ẓihār, where a man compares his wife to his mother and thereby renders marital relations unlawful until expiation is made. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام outlines the required expiatory options for each occurrence and rules separation when the man is unable to fulfill any of them.
